jobs.title: Head of Product, New Customer Experience
jobs.description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

By the Numbers:

- 500,000+ small businesses served nationwide

- Named #1 best software for small business by G2

- 2,700+ employees in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and growing

- Over $1B in annual revenue

- The SMB market is large (and growing!) with huge opportunities for Gusto to make an incredible impact for SMBs

- There are 6.2M employers in the US, 98% have fewer than 100 employees (1)

- 550,000 new businesses are created each year in the US (1)

What Product Management is like at Gusto:

- Our Product team is lean, which means you’ll have a high degree of impact and ownership. We believe in smaller, empowered teams that move quickly with less overhead. You’ll move fast by pairing sharp product judgment with fluency in AI tools — automating what slows teams down and amplifying what makes them creative and high-performing.

- We’re boundaryless builders. Lines between roles are intentionally blurred, and our PMs do whatever it takes to deliver outcomes. You’ll prototype, automate, design, and ship — using AI as your co-builder to turn problems into durable solutions that deliver customer value with urgency and care.

- We’re here to serve small and medium businesses. Gusto has a strong mission-driven culture, and we care deeply about lifting up these business owners — building technology for an AI-first world that gives them the superpowers to run and grow their businesses with confidence.

- We’re comfortable with change. Our environment moves fast, and PMs here thrive in ambiguity — blending curiosity, experimentation, and AI-native craft to shape how products (and work itself) are built at Gusto.

About the Role:

Gusto is looking for an experienced Product leader for our New Customer Experience team. Gusto is known as the trusted payroll solution for hundreds of thousands of SMBs. As we expand as the trusted small business partner with new multi-product offerings, we need to ensure new customers can clearly see, and choose, the Gusto that’s right for their business. As Head of Product, New Customer Experience, you will be responsible for the entire product experience a small business takes from potentially never having heard of Gusto, to activating the Gusto products that help them start, run, and grow. Every new Gusto customer comes through the surfaces your team owns, which makes this one of the highest-leverage product roles at the company.

About the Team:

New Customer Experience is part of Gusto's Growth organization and covers four areas: our top-of-funnel web experience, onboarding, activation, and the shared onboarding platform that other Gusto product teams build on. You will lead a team of product managers and partner daily with Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Sales, and Finance. Onboarding is genuinely hard for SMBs: tax IDs, bank verification, signatories, prior payroll history. Our job is to make that feel less like paperwork and more like being guided through it by a small business expert.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

- Ownership: You will own the end-to-end new customer experience, including determining the best way to natively include AI throughout to assist customers. Set and evangelize a strategy for how small businesses discover, evaluate, and start using Gusto, including how we show up in AI assistants and agentic surfaces, where a prospective customer may never visit our website at all.

- North Star: Create a best-in-class new customer experience which grows the number of small businesses who choose Gusto and get successfully set up - increasing acquisition volume, optimizing onboarding conversion, and establishing Gusto as the default small business partner solution.

- Collaborate: You'll work closely with every function: Engineering, Design, Data, Marketing, Sales, and Finance to bring your vision to life. You’ll rally cross-functional teams and leaders around a shared onboarding platform strategy.

- Empowerment: Directly coach and lead a talented team of senior product managers. You will raise the bar on craft, customer understanding, and execution velocity.

Here’s what we're looking for:

- 10+ years of direct Product Management experience, including 4+ years leading and managing product managers.

- A track record owning a growth, acquisition, or onboarding funnel with direct accountability for a conversion or revenue number, not just shipping features. You know your funnel numbers cold.

- Hands-on experience shipping AI-powered customer experiences. You have a real point of view on what acquisition looks like when the front door is an AI assistant rather than a website, you know how to evaluate whether an AI experience actually beats the flow it replaced, and you treat latency and cost as product constraints. You use AI in your own work to research, synthesize, and prototype.

- Experience in selling to SMBs, and experience in a multi-product company with shared platforms and real cross-team dependencies

- Experience owning a public web surface (e.g. marketing site, CMS) a plus.

- Strong experimentation instincts and the judgment to know when a flat result means iterate and when it means stop. You are a builder who stays close to the work

- Experience partnering closely with Marketing, Sales, and Finance, with direct accountability to a revenue target or P&L

If you don't think you meet all of the criteria above but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone excited to join the team.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is $206,00/yr to $248,000/yr in Denver & most major metro locations, and $243,000/yr to $292,000/yr for San Francisco, Seattle & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate location, experience, and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer .

Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to  Gusto's Applicant Privacy Notice .

Because Gusto runs payroll, we can offer banking that understands a business's largest recurring outflow from day one, while we can also meet businesses at the moment of formation, before they ever reach the payroll stage.

This is a ground-floor role. The product is early, moving toward its first beta, and this PM will help take it from initial launch through scale.

- Use Gusto's unique payroll ecosystem to build banking features unique to our positon in the ecosystem

- Define how banking connects to the rest of the Gusto platform, making the account the default funding source for how a business operates.

- Design for self-serve by anticipating where customers get stuck and resolving it in-product rather than in the support queue.

- Ensure tight, daily coordination with cross-functional teams spanning Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Ops to ship resilient, compliant, and delightful products.

- Partner with external vendors (e.g., partner banks, banking infrastructure providers, card processors) to deliver reliable, integrated experiences.

- Deeply understand our customers, particularly how cash flow uncertainty and team spending dynamics impact small business owners, and use that empathy to craft effective product narratives.

- Measure what matters — define and own KPIs around account opening, funding, deposit growth, and primacy, and use data to drive prioritization, learning, and iteration

- Has a bias toward action, comfort with ambiguity, and a strong sense of ownership.

- Has 7+ years of product management experience in fintech, banking, or adjacent industries.

- Brings hands-on familiarity with business banking, BaaS platforms, deposit products, or money movement rails — bonus for experience with KYB/onboarding flows, ledgering, or partner bank relationships.

- Thrives in 0→1 environments and knows how to take a product from pre-beta to launch with limited resources.

- Has run a real experimentation practice — hypothesis, test design, readout, decision — and knows how to learn from directional signal when a new product doesn't yet have the volume for statistical significance.

- Understands the regulatory and operational complexity of banking products and can partner effectively with Risk, Legal, and Compliance teams.

- Cares deeply about small businesses and wants to build the account they trust with their money.

- Use Gusto's unique position in the payroll ecosystem to build consumer features that can only be built at the origination of income

- Deeply understand our customers, particularly hourly and salaried workforces to craft product narratives and help create real financial progress.

- Get in the trenches with cross-functional teams spanning Product, Engineering, Design, Data, Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Ops to ship resilient, compliant, and delightful products.

- Has familiarity with AI tools and comfortable using AI tools, including prototypes to accelerate the development lifecycle.

- Is data oriented and experienced using data to inform decisions and track outcomes

- Brings meaningful familiarity with accounting concepts (journal entries, reconciliation flows) and can ramp quickly into the accounting product space.

- Is comfortable facing ambiguous problems.

- Is able to wear multiple hats, for example conducting user research, forecasting product adoption or prototyping a new feature all in the same week

- Can understand not just how an individual feature works, but how it fits into the broader accounting system.

- Is comfortable working through detailed workflows, edge cases, data mappings, ledger concepts, and controls needed for accountant confidence.

- Should have strong frameworks/foundations to meaningfully prioritize and deliver on customer needs and business outcomes.
